## Tange et al. (2009), pressure-scale-free Fit3 Vinet-MGD

Record: `mgo_b1_tange_2009_vinet` · Model: `Vinet`

**Outcome: Numerically similar, with qualifications.**

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization.
**Comparison basis:** Every compared free coefficient meets either the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison or parameter-specific numerical similarity screen; the audit does not classify the complete comparison as parity.

[Stored EOS coefficients and source](../material-summaries/mgo.md#record-mgo_b1_tange_2009_vinet)

### What this result establishes

**Separate source-review status:** primary\_source\_validated.
**Usage recommendation:** See the stored EOS qualifications; no recommendation is inferred here.

- The 164-row approximate reconstruction recovers all four independent Fit 3 coefficients within the numerical similarity limits, including over the tested 1-3% Zha-weight range. It is classified as similar, not parity, because the exact Zha rows and legacy weights are unpublished, one Fiquet state is unresolved, the Zha block is curve-based, and the restricted local inputs are not redistributed.
- This named numerical assessment alone does not establish author-workflow reproduction, physical accuracy or recommendation for use.

### Data and reconstruction method

- **Dataset identifiers:** mgo\_dubrovinsky\_1997\_cod\_thermal\_expansion; mgo\_fiquet\_1999\_cod\_thermal\_expansion; mgo\_li\_2006\_table1\_elasticity; mgo\_marsh\_1980\_lasl\_single\_crystal\_hugoniot
- **Observations:** 164
- **Fit kind:** approximate\_coupled\_vinet\_mgd\_global\_reconstruction
- **Objective:** source-weighted thermal, elastic, and shock residuals
- **Free parameters:** K0\_prime; a; b; gamma0
- **Fixed parameters:** V0; n

Unspecified selections, weights, fixed values or error conventions remain unknown; they have not been inferred for this report.

### Curves, residuals and fit error

**Partial replay — available subsets only.**

PARTIAL REPLAY: these panels evaluate both stored coefficient sets only on the public bundled thermal-expansion, Li elastic and LASL shock subsets. The two dependent reference parameters are recomputed using the same documented thermodynamic constraints. RMS values apply only to the individually named public subsets.

<a id="record-mgo_li_2006_bm3_absolute_acoustic"></a>

## Li et al. (2006), acoustic absolute-pressure BM3

Record: `mgo_li_2006_bm3_absolute_acoustic` · Model: `BM3`

**Outcome: Numerically similar, with qualifications.**

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization.
**Comparison basis:** Every compared free coefficient meets either the recorded combined-two-sigma comparison or parameter-specific numerical similarity screen; the audit does not classify the complete comparison as parity.

[Stored EOS coefficients and source](../material-summaries/mgo.md#record-mgo_li_2006_bm3_absolute_acoustic)

### What this result establishes

**Separate source-review status:** primary\_source\_validated.
**Usage recommendation:** See the stored EOS qualifications; no recommendation is inferred here.

- Direct reproduction of the source measurement-to-coefficient chain, not a pressure-volume refit: the preferred decompression density, VP, and VS rows plus the independently measured ambient anchor are fitted to the published third-order acoustic finite-strain equations. Equation 4 then maps the fitted adiabatic K0S and K0S-prime to the stored isothermal K0T and K0T-prime; paragraph 10's K0T-in-L2/M2 approximation accounts for the measured isothermal strains. The calculated Table 1 pressures are downstream BM3 outputs and are never used as observations. The source does not publish its exact weights, iterative adiabatic-foot correction, covariance, or propagated isothermal errors, so the unweighted rounded-table reconstruction is classified as numerically similar rather than strict parity.
- This named numerical assessment alone does not establish author-workflow reproduction, physical accuracy or recommendation for use.

### Data and reconstruction method

- **Dataset identifiers:** mgo\_li\_2006\_table1\_elasticity
- **Observations:** 11
- **Fit kind:** acoustic\_finite\_strain\_then\_isothermal\_conversion
- **Selection:** Section 2 ambient density/VP/VS anchor plus all ten Table 1 decompression-after-annealing density/VP/VS rows
- **Objective:** unweighted simultaneous VP and VS residuals in km/s
- **Absolute sigma:** False
- **Free parameters:** K0; K0\_prime
- **Fixed parameters:** V0

Unspecified selections, weights, fixed values or error conventions remain unknown; they have not been inferred for this report.

<a id="record-mgo_shen_2026_vinet_3"></a>

## Shen and Smith (2026), Cu-referenced Vinet

Record: `mgo_shen_2026_vinet_3` · Model: `Vinet`

**Outcome: Parity not achieved for this comparison.**

**Scope:** Comparison with the source parameterization.
**Comparison basis:** Direct reconstruction from source observations: each Table S1 phase volume is paired with its simultaneous Cu volume, pressure is evaluated from Fratanduono et al.'s analytic third-order 298 K Vinet fit, and K0 and K0\_prime are fitted with Shen and Smith's fixed V0 and stated run selection. The source publishes no pressure weights, residual covariance, or weighting protocol, so the reproduction uses unweighted pressure residuals and does not infer any of them. The paper identifies Table II as direct fits to this study's Cu-referenced P-V data, with earlier literature included for comparison. Its data-availability statement also mentions other author-held data, so completeness of the actual author fit inputs is unconfirmed. No additional experimental fit rows are identified by the published fitting description. See the \[source-input audit\](literature-reproductions/shen-smith-2026-cu-refits.md). Not recommended for scientific predictions or pressure calibration. Retained only for explicit diagnostic inspection. The published fixed-V0 MgO Vinet curve gives 1.161241 GPa pressure RMS and residuals up to +2.8032 GPa on all 194 DAC-2 Table S1 observations. A direct unweighted refit gives K0=161.827434 GPa, K0\_prime=3.953583 and RMS 0.475879 GPa, versus published 161.9 GPa and 4.08. The source-fit discrepancy is unresolved.

[Stored EOS coefficients and source](../material-summaries/mgo.md#record-mgo_shen_2026_vinet_3)

### Curves, residuals and fit error

![Original/source and refitted curves with pressure residuals for mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3](figures/mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3-curves.svg#only-light)
![Original/source and refitted curves with pressure residuals for mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3](figures/mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3-curves-dark.svg#only-dark)

| Fit | Pressure RMS error (GPa) |
| --- | ---: |
| Original / source fit | 3.34 |
| Reconstruction / refit | 0.0194 |

Both fits use the same 8 recovered audit input rows. Residual = P(model) − P(input), evaluated at each input volume and temperature (isothermal records use their reference temperature). RMS is an unweighted descriptive pressure error, not a parameter uncertainty or the optimizer's weighted/latent-coordinate objective.

**Volume coordinate:** volume\_ratio. **Row selection:** all rows; reference-T rows.

Curves use full stored coefficients. For thermal data, separate isotherms are labelled; when there are more than five temperatures, the minimum, middle and maximum sampled temperatures are shown. Residuals include every selected row at its own temperature. Coordinate error bars appear only where the row reader can recover all widths; their meaning remains that of the source dataset (including digitization widths). Missing bars do not mean zero error. No uncertainty band is inferred.

### Source versus reconstruction

![Source/target and reconstructed central values for mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3](figures/mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3.svg#only-light)
![Source/target and reconstructed central values for mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3](figures/mgo_belmonte_2017_b3lyp_static_bm3-dark.svg#only-dark)

This is a **coefficient comparison**, not an observation or residual plot.
Each panel uses its coefficient's audit units and includes zero. Markers show
stored central values and available recorded error widths (also in the table below);
